newsitem.title: HONG KONG: French spiderman scales Hong Kong skyscraper.
newsitem.headline: French spiderman scales Hong Kong skyscraper.

text.p: A French daredevil nicknamed the spiderman scaled the shimmering golden facade of one of Hong Kong's tallest skyscrapers on Wednesday, eluding security guards and police until he reached the top of the 48-storey tower.
Shunning equipment, Alain Robert, a 34-year-old Parisian, took just half an hour to get to the summit of the Far East Finance Centre in Hong Kong's Admiralty business district.
Robert, wearing a black T-shirt and jeans, scaled his way up by supporting himself on window rims and straddling between panes as he ascended, hardly stopping for breath.
Bystanders gasped in awe, pointing to what looked like a black spot moving up the golden glass facade. Firemen called to the scene also kept a close watch on proceedings.

On reaching the peak of the tower block, Robert raised his arms in victory. An experienced rock climber, he told reporters he had also climbed other structures around the world, including San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge.
Robert was later taken away for questioning by police, who said he might be charged for "disorderly conduct".
